newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-HODDLE'S SUBS EARN NEW CHANCE.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-HODDLE'S SUBS EARN NEW CHANCE.

text.p: Several members of the makeshift England side who beat Mexico 2-0 in a friendly at Wembley on Saturday did enough to stake strong claims for World Cup places, according to manager Glenn Hoddle.
Georgia visit Wembley for a group two qualifying match on April 30 and some of the players who might have been thought to have been making up the numbers against Mexico could get another outing.

"Opportunities are always there to stake a claim,'' said Hoddle. "Rob Lee did well attacking and defensively. Robbie Fowler started a little bit nervously, but he's still got a lot to learn at this level. He got off the mark in international football and that's a burden off his shoulders.
"And David James made his debut in goal, and there's a bit of pressure on you when you make your debut, so he will be better for that.

"People have to challenge other people, and if there are people challenging for an England shirt that's good for the coach. The one in the international shirt can't take his foot off the pedal and the others are pushing to get in,'' Hoddle added.
He said the game had given him a chance to use a new system, with Graeme Le Saux playing in a back four when the opponents were attacking but pushing into the midfield when England had the ball.
"Playing that way was a lot of hard work for Graeme, and he did well. It proves he's firmly back to full fitness.''
Despite knocks to Lee (ankle) and Teddy Sheringham, who left the pitch before half-time with concussion, Hoddle said his squad would return to their clubs in fine fettle.
